contract.interface:
Source-reported candidate theorem: for every integer r>=1, an explicit rational finite continuous-time Markov chain Q_r with 4r<=n<=16r, uniform stationary law and balanced binary observation Y_t=f(X_t) has an exponentially hard passive distinction from a stationary equilibrium binary chain of flip rate 1/2, but a polynomial-duration test under a specified conservative-field rate law. All statements use ordinary stationary time reversal with every microscopic state even under physical reversal. Independent correctness and historical priority remain UNKNOWN; no device or transformative technological capability is established.

The positive Walsh lift is Q_r=J-I+epsilon A, epsilon=1/(16r), A^3=0, rank(A)=2r and ||A||_(2->2)=1. With ell=2r-1 and distinct Walsh characters {1,f,c_1,...,c_ell,d_1,...,d_ell}, d_j=f c_j, set Af=d_1, A c_j=d_(j+1) for j<ell, A c_ell=f, and A zero on other characters. A1=A*1=0, ||A||_F^2=2r and ||A-A*||_F^2=4r. The explicit state-basis construction gives 7/(8n)<=q_ij<=9/(8n), exit rate <9/8, reverse-rate ratio <=9/7, total-variation mixing <=exp(-t/2), and all nonzero eigenvalues -1 with Jordan blocks of size at most three. An actual label-preserving state permutation R satisfies RQR=Q*, ensuring an exactly time-reversal-invariant observed path law. R is an auxiliary symmetry, not an alternative physical reversal convention. The source bounds sigma(Q_r) between 1/(144r) and 1/(112r).

Multiplication Dg=fg switches 1 with f and c_j with d_j. A scalar observation word containing A needs at least 2r A-insertions and 2r+1 observations. All joint distributions at <=2r times match the binary equilibrium reference, including C(t)=exp(-t). The first odd moment at t_0<...<t_(2r) is epsilon^(2r) exp[-(t_(2r)-t_0)] product_j(t_j-t_(j-1))>0. This observation-depth statement alone is not the full passive lower bound.

For full continuous records, Q_r=(J-I)/2+B with B=(J-I)/2+epsilon A a valid uniform-stationary generator. Give the observer the independent rate-1/2 reset times as extra information. On each segment the projection/Duhamel series has no contributions of orders 1,...,2r-1, and the state-basis row norm K<=2r bounds the remaining signed terms. The source obtains TV(P_Q^[0,T],P_eq^[0,T])<=(2/3)(1+T/2)16^(-r), covering exact jump times and unlimited processing. Equal-prior success >=2/3 therefore requires the fixed observation horizon T>=16^r-2. This is not a lower bound on expected sequential stopping time. For M independently acquired stationary windows of total length T the bound becomes (2/3)(M+T/2)16^(-r); stationary starts are not free resources. Scaling both generators by r gives sigma in [1/144,1/112], passive horizon >=(16^r-2)/r, controlled unit trial duration 1/r and exit rates O(r).

Essential active interface: q_ij^(h)=q_ij exp[h(f_j-f_i)/2], with diagonal row sums restored, initial zero-field stationarity and symmetric kinetic factors fixed. This law is not determined by passive observations or guaranteed by simply naming a field. The source derives chi_r(t)=1-exp(-t)-(epsilon^2/2)[1-(1+t)exp(-t)], versus chi_eq(t)=1-exp(-t). At t=1 the gap is c_* epsilon^2, c_*=(1-2/e)/2>1/8. Take h=epsilon/100 and finite difference D(h)=[m(h)-m(-h)]/(2h); a third-derivative bound <500 yields bias <=500h^2/6 and a finite-field gap >=13epsilon^2/120>epsilon^2/10. The equilibrium mean is tanh(h)[1-exp(-cosh(h))].

To acquire that distinction rather than assume a susceptibility oracle, estimate each endpoint mean to a=epsilon^3/8000 using N=ceil[(2/a^2)log(8/zeta)] samples per sign. Before every trial, switch the field off and wait L>=2log(8N/zeta); regeneration coupling charges dependent-trial error. The claimed total experiment duration is O(r^6 log(1/zeta)[1+log(r/zeta)]), including the waits, with inverse-polynomial absolute field/timing tolerances epsilon^3/10^8 and polynomially many precision bits. The constants are conservative and large. The archive contains no Monte Carlo implementation of this full sampling protocol. A bound of 2|h| on field-switch work per trial excludes actuator, sensor, calibration and model-construction costs and establishes no total energy advantage.

To exclude a dispensable hidden dissipative subsystem, the source constructs F_+=product_(j=1)^r Y_j and F_-=product_(j=1)^r Y_(-j) with conditional covariance -tau_r given Y_0=-1, tau_r=epsilon^(2r)exp(-2r). Finite reversible hidden deterministic-observation models have nonnegative conditional past/future covariance. For any finite stationary all-even exact hidden realization G, additive reversibilization G_rev=(G+G^dagger)/2 has the same stationary law and exit rates and KL(P_G^L||P_Grev^L)<=L sigma(G)/4. A bounded covariance witness and Pinsker imply sigma(G)>=epsilon^(4r)exp(-4r)/(16r)>0, uniformly over finite hidden dimension and rates. This floor is not sharp and does not estimate the actual dissipation to fixed relative error.

For a finite stationary generator and bounded f under the same rate-perturbation law, the note proposes |chi(t)-[C(0)-C(t)]|^2<=(M^2/2)sigma t Var(f), M=(max f-min f)/2. Balanced binary observations give sigma>=2|response defect|^2/t; the constructed t=1 response supplies an inverse-polynomial floor 2c_*^2 epsilon^4 for models matching both correlation and susceptibility. Promoting finite differences to this derivative certificate also requires a controlled Taylor remainder. This is neither a universal response oracle nor a universal hidden-system inference algorithm.

Resources and robustness: a dense explicit generator uses O(n^2 log(r+2)) bits and O(r n^2) character operations to construct; output and acquisition are charged, not polylogarithmic in r. The exporter uses signed 64-bit integer arrays with overflow guards and quadratic dense output. Reflection-paired ladder amplitudes in [1/2,1] preserve the stated separation up to constants; generic microscopic errors can create shorter observation loops. Realizing the dense rates, justifying the field response, measuring small signals, calibrating errors, optimizing sample complexity and characterizing broad efficient observable/control algebras remain unresolved.

Prior credits are preserved explicitly: Skinner--Dunkel arXiv:2011.08765 for dissipation inference from apparently time-symmetric coarse graining; Cugliandolo--Dean--Kurchan cond-mat/9705002 for response/entropy-production connections; Shiraishi arXiv:2609.34352v1 for the eigenvalue-only counterexample; and the unreviewed ipitchford/hidden-dissipation-floor research candidate v1.1 for additive reversibilization and conditional past/future comparisons. The latter tools are reproved here; its broader claims are not imported as independently established theorems. No Astra or OpenAI/math theorem is a premise, and no topical link is promoted to a proof dependency. Combined historical priority has not been established.
